item.content:encoded:
Timer expired. Edits made.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team.

This is an article that has a lot going on in the development of the anomalous entity, which goes from having a very distinct mode of function and effect, to possibly having some sort of underlying reason for the effect that it does have though it isn't completely understood. As to not disrupt the flow of the article, I'm proposing a link to the dossier that was made for Site-77, within the dossier is a complete list of all the scips in containment at the site so readers that are directed there from this article would have a lot of other articles to choose from, which is a great avenue for wiki-walking.

Editing this:

SCP-213 is contained in a high security humanoid containment cell within Site-77.

To read:

SCP-213 is contained in a high security humanoid containment cell within Site-77.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: Is it really a Sue?
item.content:encoded: Any time there are humans with powers, especially young adults/teens, many people call out Mary Sue/Marty Stu. It's not always like that, yes it happens a lot, but not always. If it was an alien that doesn't look human, this probably wouldn't be accused of being one, at worst it would be accused of being unoriginal, but not a Sue.

I know I couldn't give less of a crap. The eyes on the palms make me think of Pan's Labyrinth, but I'm not gonna throw a hissy fit over it. Someone else linked to a tvtropes page which (someone else counted) has 61 different examples of eyes in weird places. Aside from all that, I'm sure Stephen King wasn't the first person to ever think about a story involving vaporizing crap as an ability.

The comment about 173 being a Boo from Mario Bros made me laugh, not have fanrage at someone stealing the idea of looking at something making it not move. The connection made me chuckle. That's it. All the anger in previous posts is imo, frankly stupid.

Also of note to Roget's words there… It's +53 with my vote just now, and that's with it having been in the negatives most of the time with those previous revisions. His edit isn't riding the coattails of the old versions, it brought it out of the dust, in a manner of speaking. =)

Having read this finally and gone through the posts from the years past I'd say this isn't as terrible as everyone has put it out to be (with this rewrite, I haven't seen the "horrible" version)

I'd actually like to see the parasite transfer to a new host after killing the current one, IMO that would make the article more interesting, open it to new containment procedures such as having to feed it a new D class now and then to keep it from actively seeking new hosts while keeping the powers it grants under Foundation control. Just my thoughts though, thinking along the lines of how parasites work in host organisms, once they become useless they move on right? Or…..multiply (evil laughter)

But over all this is ok. For now I’ll save my vote, maybe come back after a while and see if anything changes.
